newsitem.title: PERU: Peru declares Yauricocha mine auction void.
newsitem.headline: Peru declares Yauricocha mine auction void.

text.p: The Peruvian government declared void Monday's intended auction of state-run polymetallic mine Yauricocha after receiving no bids, Energy and Mines Ministry officials said.
Ten companies from countries including Peru, Canada and Mexico had bought bidding details ahead of the auction.
The officials did not say when the mine would be offered again.
Yauricocha, which lies 220 miles (350 km) southeast of Lima, had a base price of $10 million and a minimum investment requirement of $18 million within three years.
The mine currently produces 30,000 tonnes of mineral per month, has proven and probable reserves of 2.8 million tonnes and potential reserves of six million tonnes.

The proven reserves have grades of 1.1 percent for copper, 2.8 percent for lead and 5.3 percent for zinc. The mineral also contains 132 grams of silver and 0.8 grams of gold per tonne, according to Centromin.
Yauricocha's auction had been intended as part of the ongoing piecemeal privatization of state mining company Centromin.
In July, the state miner launched its sell-off with the successful sale of two of the company's major assets.
First, a Canadian consortium of Rio Algom Ltd and Inmet Mining Corp agreed to invest $2.52 billion over the next five years to become owner of the copper-rich Antamina prospect.

Also, Canada's Barrick Gold Corporation won the option to buy Peru's Quicay gold prospect by offering at an auction to pay $202 million should the company decide to develop the asset after feasibility studies.
The government plans to sell Centromin's seven mines, its La Oroya metallurgical complex, a railroad network, port facilities, four hydroelectric plants and several prospects by the middle of 1997.
